newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish government allies in slander battle.
newsitem.headline: Turkish government allies in slander battle.

text.p: A court has ordered one of Turkey's coalition partners to pay the other $40,000 compensation in a slander case highlighting the oddball nature of the ruling Islamist-led alliance.

Pro-Western secularist Tansu Ciller was found guilty on Wednesday of unjustly damaging the character of Necmettin Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader, in an acrimonious pre-election television debate last year.
Ciller, now Erbakan's deputy, had labelled him a heroin trafficker. The pair did not consider scrapping the case despite working closely together since June, aides said.

"It has to continue to the end because people might get the wrong idea," Ciller aide Hasan Ekinci told Reuters. "There was a serious allegation that has to be cleared up in line with respect for the law," he said.
The case has automatically gone to the appeals court where it may linger for another year. "She will definitely pay if she has to," Ekinci said.
He said Erbakan would probably give the money to a charity.
Former prime minister Ciller had vowed not to let the Islamists into government but she caved in under pressure of corruption charges that are still hanging over her.
Erbakan's Welfare Party has the power to acquit Ciller of the graft accusations.
